question.text: Saraswati Growth Fund, a Cat II AIF set up as a trust, earns INR 8 crore characterised as 'business income' during FY 2024-25 (pre-FA 2025 amendment period). Which of the following statements correctly describes the tax treatment of this business income stream?

answer.text: Business income is taxed at the fund level at MMR (since the AIF is a trust), exempt in investor hands, and any business loss is not passed through but carried forward at fund level.
Business income is also passed through to unitholders under the same Section 10(23FBA) mechanism.
Business income is exempt at both fund and investor level because the fund is registered with SEBI.
Business income is taxed at 12.5% at the fund level with indexation benefits.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBB) carves business income OUT of the pass-through regime. Where the AIF is a trust or LLP, business income is taxed at the fund level at MMR (i.e., the rate applicable to the highest slab of an individual/AOP/BOI in the Finance Act, currently ~39% effective). The income is then exempt in investor hands. Business losses cannot be passed through — they remain at the fund level and carry forward for set-off against future business income. The Trap: Option A ignores the Section 10(23FBB) carve-out. Option B treats all AIF income as exempt, which is incorrect — only non-business income is pass-through. Option D applies the LTCG rate to business income, mixing two separate regimes. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this dual regime (pass-through for non-business + fund-level MMR for business) as the defining feature of Cat I/II taxation. XIX-A tests it at the LP-disclosure level. Note: FA 2025 amended Sec 2(14) to deem securities held by Cat I/II AIFs as capital assets, shrinking the business-income exposure from FY 2025-26 onward. Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Cat II debt-fund Manager, drafting the investment strategy as 'hold-to-maturity credit' rather than 'active credit trading' materially reduces business-income risk. Document the hold-period analysis in the IC memo — GAAR and case-by-case characterisation still look at facts, not labels.
